chapter: The craft of the ad lib player
title: Mingus, Ellington and Charlie Parker
summary: Hall calls Mingus avant garde and says Ellington is the basis of all the music while Parker modernised it.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What do you think about Mingus' contributions?
Fine, but that was more avant garde. He had to have a special kind of listener. I'm not speaking about his dexterity or his -- he was a genius for what he was doing.

But, you know, he was so -- also influenced by Duke Ellington and Charlie Parker, and a lot of his music reflects that, you know, as well as some of the things that were, you know, avant garde at the time, but I
think in subsequent bands he, you know, used a lot of the influence of Duke Ellington and Charlie Parker.

Well, the influence -- the influence of Charlie -- of Duke Ellington is the basic -- the basis of the music that we played. So anything that you do is an influence of Duke Ellington. Charlie Parker went to a different level, modernized it, genius nevertheless, But it was a different -- a different mode of -- 'Black Lady' -- you could relate to Duke Ellington and Fats Waller and Fletcher Henderson in bands of that period, but -- and sit back and relax and listen to it.
But when Charlie Parker started with and Diz their's, you'd have to sit at the front of your seat to listen, which doesn't mean that you're relaxed. You're just a listener then.
